messages:
incident-bot: Incident opened: Unhealthy model artifact fetches from Hugging Face (429 rate caps observed). Auto-alert triggered by 5xx/429 spike on model-fetch metric. Paging oncall-ml and oncall-sre.
oncall-ml: seeing ~18% of model fetches failing with 429s at the artifact layer. Cold-starts are spiking because the model download step is getting rate-limited.
oncall-sre: thanks. are these for a single HF endpoint or many?
oncall-ml: looks like a subset - manifests and blobs for 4 models in registry-ms (mainly larger LLMs). HF response includes Retry-After headers in some cases.
eng-runtime-lead: quick note: request path failing is /hf-storage/objects/{sha} when pulling from hf.s3.backed-hosting. We have local artifact-cache but TTL is short; many lanes still cold.
prod-support: Customer impact report: C-Enterprise (50k qps) experiencing 502s in our API gateway when model-fetch fails during cold-starts; estimated 6% of user requests affected in last 30m. Will confirm with telemetry.
hf-status-bot: Hugging Face status page: "Partial service degradation - model hosting rate limit" https://status.huggingface.co/incidents/xyz (posted).
oncall-sre: ok, immediate mitigations to consider: 1) increase local cache TTL to force serving from mirror where available; 2) route new cold-starts to quantized small-model variants; 3) bulk prefetch for warm pools.
eng-runtime-lead: implementing cache TTL bump now via feature flag ramp. Doing a 10x increase for cached manifests and blobs in artifact-proxy. Pushing config in 120s.
oncall-ml: starting smart-prefetch job to warm most-requested model shards to the dedicated artifact pool (low-priority job). ETA ~8m.
infra-ops: adding temporary rate-limited mirror host to edge CDN (we have a partial mirror in GCS from previous sync). Will create a routing rule to prefer internal mirror if origin returns 429. Doing this now.
prod-support: posting customer advisory: "We are aware of degraded model load times and intermittent 5xx for some customers. Engineers investigating. No data loss." Ask CS to prepare a short note for top customers.
customer-success: drafting message for affected enterprise tenants. will include expected mitigations and ETA once prefetch status confirmed.
oncall-sre: small checklist while mitigations run: 
- add retry-with-backoff (exponential) on fetcher with jitter (we already have but need to relax failure budget)
- reduce parallel fetch workers per instance to avoid thundering herd
- enable HF 429-aware retry (honor Retry-After header)
- enable fallback to smaller model if manifest fetch fails for >10s
eng-runtime-lead: code snippet I'm pushing now to limiter config (rolling to all runtime nodes):
```yaml
artifact_cache:
  manifest_ttl: 3600 # was 300
  blob_ttl: 86400 # was 3600
fetcher:
  max_parallel_fetches: 2 # was 8
  retry:
    attempts: 6
    backoff_base_ms: 200
    honor_retry_after: true
```
noncall-ml: prefetched top 20 shards for model redwood/gtr-large-2025 to artifact-pool-1. Warm pool size increasing.
hf-status-bot: update: HF acknowledges elevated rate limiting; "We're working to increase throughput. Some customers on shared hosting may see throttles." (link).
oncall-sre: we should also scope customer impact quant: from logs, ~4.8% of total inference requests incurred downstream model-fetch latency >5s causing gateway timeouts. Marking severity P2 -> potential to go P1 if impact grows.
prod-support: opening incident page and adding timeline. Adding affected customers list and contact points.
oncall-ml: testing fallback path: if manifest fetch fails, runtime will skip warm-start and spin a fast-quant variant (smaller). Doing a staged rollout to 10% traffic for impacted routes.
eng-runtime-lead: feature flag rollout at 10% now. watching errors.
infra-ops: mirror routing in place: artifact-proxy now prefers internal-gcs-mirror on origin 429. Added header X-Artifact-Source to responses for tracing.
oncall-sre: also please capture HF Retry-After values in metrics; plotting now.
prod-support: CS notified three customers directly (enterprise contacts). One replied: they can tolerate degraded perf but want hourly updates.
eng-runtime-lead: early telemetry: error rate dropped from 18% -> 6% after TTL bump + mirror routing + prefetch. Latency for cold-starts reduced by ~1.8s median.
noncall-ml: still seeing some 429s for very large shard downloads (~1GB). HF is rate-limiting chunked downloads. Recommending we cap per-file concurrency and enable chunked resume.
eng-runtime-lead: rolling patch to fetcher to limit per-file connections to 1 and enable ranged-get resume. Deploying now.
hf-status-bot: HF status update: "Mitigation in progress, rate limits increasing. We recommend customers use mirrors for bulk transfers."
noncall-sre: plan recap: 1) TTL bump permanent until HF confirms stable 2) keep mirror routing 3) keep fallback-to-small-model feature enabled for affected routes 4) patch fetcher for ranged-get resume 5) follow up with HF support for rate quota increase for our org if available
prod-support: creating post-incident channel and scheduling 1-hour incident review in 3 hours. Include runtime, infra, ML, and CS.
customer-success: asked HF support for expected window and any quota bump options. HF responded "Working on mitigation; we'll follow up with org-level options."
oncall-ml: preliminary customer impact: spike lasted ~38m, peak error rate ~18%, total affected requests ~2.4% of daily volume but concentrated on heavy-model tenants.
oncall-sre: switching oncall: @oncall-ml will remain primary, @oncall-sre will hand to next shift at +45m. Please annotate handoff in timeline.
oncall-ml: acknowledged. staying.
eng-runtime-lead: adding runbook task list to incident doc: review cache policies, add tests for HF 429 behavior, add permanent mirror sync job, and add capability to pre-warm based on usage forecasts.
prod-support: logging final mitigation state: TTL bump + mirror routing + prefetch + ranged-get = stable for now. Continuing to monitor.
incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, severity=P2, duration=0h45m.
customer-success: will send consolidated update to affected customers now.
eng-runtime-lead: will follow up on postmortem items after incident review.
noncall-sre: thanks all. if HF fully resolves and our error rate stays <1% for 1h we'll close.
prod-support: will close when criteria met.
incident-bot: Incident closed by oncall-sre (closing note: mitigations held; HF is scaling; follow-up: permanent mirror + runbook).
